plan.title: Liver drug treatment: 3v3 DESeq2 DE + power caveat + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: Three treated vs three control liver samples, raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples used; metadata table has 6 rows). Design is unpaired, single-batch, minimal replication. The plan follows the grounded procedure for this exact situation (2-group, n=3/3, salmon counts, human, no batch): sample-structure QC first to catch any outlier or non-clustering sample before the model is trusted; minimal pre-filter; DESeq2 Wald test as primary DE model with apeglm-shrunk log2FC, edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as an independent cross-check (both control FDR at n=3 per the cited benchmark; the intersection becomes the high-confidence gene set); Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering at alpha=0.05; apeglm shrinkage for ranking/plotting; fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome (both staged locally) since with n=3 the significant-gene list is likely too short for a reliable over-representation test; and a final report step that states explicitly, per the grounded rule, the statistical power limitation of an n=3-per-group design (a minority of true DE genes recovered, biased toward large fold changes; a gene absent from the list is not evidence of no effect) alongside full method/version/threshold documentation and fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram).

fgsea preranked on Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome
